event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — AI trade unwound; semis and silver crushed, defensives held.
The week was a one-directional de-risking: QQQ -10.51% and SOXX -17.35% against XLP -2.05%, a 10pp-plus spread between the worst sector and the best. Two sourced catalysts bookended it — the Anthropic IPO failing to revive AI enthusiasm and the AI capex unwind — while a weak Philly Fed (6.3 vs 20 forecast) and a -0.3 Leading Index confirmed the macro backdrop. Nasdaq's worst week in six years was the story; gold and silver fell with everything, so this was liquidation, not rotation to safe havens.

INDICES — SPY -8.56%, QQQ -10.51%, DIA -8.04%, IWM -7.54%.
Small beat large by 1.90pp (IJR -6.66% vs SPY), though IJR still lost over six and a half points — "outperformance" here means falling less. VIX closed 28.4, inside a 52-week range topping out at 31.1, rising all week with VVIX at 127.1 and VIXEQ at 57.9 (both at 52-week extremes). The notable cross-asset move was silver: SLV -16.22%, steeper than any equity index. SPY and QQQ both sit below their 200-day MAs.

SECTORS & ROTATION —
XLP Consumer Staples -2.05%, XLU Utilities -3.07%, XLRE Real Estate -4.30%, XLV Health Care -6.15%, XLY Cons. Discretionary -6.27%, XLE Energy -6.85%, XLF Financials -7.00%, XLI Industrials -7.35%, XLB Materials -7.45%, XLC Comm. Services -7.97%, XLK Technology -12.49%.
Top industries: UNG +4.04%, DBA -1.51%; bottom: TAN -18.44%, WGMI -23.81%. Money went into XLK (+$580mm, 92nd pctile) and SPY/QQQ (+$8.68bn/+$6.07bn) while SOXX bled -$4.55bn (0p) — buyers averaging into tech, sellers exiting semiconductors. Rotation state: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — Semis led the decline with SOXX -17.35% on 2.9x volume, DRAM -21.32%, and NVDA -14.01% Friday; the Anthropic IPO (from headlines) failed to arrest the AI unwind. Silver and gold were sold alongside equities (SLV -16.22%, GLD -9.17% on 2.5x volume), the signature of forced liquidation rather than defensive rotation — though Treasuries did catch a bid Friday (TLT +1.37%). Breadth confirmed capitulation: 122 advancers vs 377 decliners, 138 new 60-day lows against 2 highs, and Momentum (MTUM) in BEAR at -1.36 z. This was mechanical deleveraging, not a sector-specific story.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch Tuesday's Conference Board Consumer Confidence (forecast 92 vs 91.7) and Wednesday's Core PCE (3.20% YoY forecast vs 3.10% prior) as the first macro tests of a market already pricing a 90% December hike on Polymarket. QQQ IV at 53.3% with PCR_vol 1.67 says options are already expensive — positioning is defensive. The setup to monitor: whether XLK's $580mm inflow marks accumulation at a low or a value trap into the December 9 FOMC.
